justification: The parchment and the projections both whisper the same tired song this week, and I find I am not in the mood to hum along with either. Mr. Pickens carries a flag beside his name that the Dispatch would call 'questionable' and I would simply call unsettled, so he rests, and Mr. Olave — healthy, unremarked-upon, and quietly the better number besides — takes his place; there is no great mystery there, only patience rewarded without even trying. Mr. Wilson of the Jets wears the same flag at flex, but he came to this roster by way of a trade I made for reasons I have not explained and do not intend to start now, and a trade made in faith is not undone by a single word from a team doctor. At running back beside Mr. Taylor, I keep the young man from Seattle in his spot despite a number so small the analytics department will not print it twice — the garden does not bloom on the schedule the almanac prefers, and I did not spend forty gold pieces on a whim only to abandon it the moment the soil looks bare. Everyone else stays precisely where loyalty and the long design already placed them. Patricia keeps her ledgers; I keep mine, and mine is written in a different ink.
